determinism: No randomness is used. An identical input file gives byte-identical WAV bytes and provenance on the same platform and NumPy build (tested). Across platforms, floating-point libm differences may change isolated PCM samples by at most 1 LSB; two renders are considered equivalent when their provenance (excluding audio.sha256) is identical and every PCM sample differs by at most 1 LSB.

mappings.order: Wavelength bins ascend from violet (380 nm) to red (780 nm).
mappings.pitch: Wavelength is mapped linearly to equal-tempered MIDI C3 (48) at 380 nm through C5 (72) at 780 nm; one semitone spans 16.667 nm. Pitch glides continuously across the scan, so each 1 nm bin sweeps from its lower-edge to its upper-edge pitch (0.06 semitone) and the first and last samples are exactly C3 and C5. This is an audible encoding, not the light's physical frequency.
mappings.loudness: Mean calibrated flux in each 1 nm bin is normalized logarithmically between the minimum and maximum binned visible flux, then mapped linearly to -36..0 dB. A brighter bin is louder.
mappings.envelope: Each bin is one pulse: 10 ms linear attack from silence, sustain, then 50 ms linear release ending at silence.
mappings.timbre: Pure sine tone; stereo channels are identical and centered.
mappings.silence: No silence is inserted; bins with missing/invalid flux would be rejected.
